_source.publisher: Annenberg Public Policy Center, University of Pennsylvania — Annenberg Constitution Day Civics Survey
_source.whyCheckedIn: APPC publishes topline PDFs only (no data endpoint) and annenbergpublicpolicycenter.org sits behind a Cloudflare challenge that blocks plain fetchers. Values transcribed from the CIVI3/CIVI4 summary table (2022 appendix p.2), the 2023 topline CIVI4 table, and the 2025 topline 'Number of Branches Correctly Recalled' table. A new topline appears each September around Constitution Day (Sept 17).

meta.name: Can Name All Three Branches of Government
meta.unit: percent of adults naming all three branches (online panel)
meta.source: Annenberg Public Policy Center, Constitution Day Civics Survey
meta.note: "Would you mind naming any of them, the three branches of government?" — percent of all respondents naming executive, legislative, and judicial, from APPC's annual Constitution Day survey (SSRS Opinion Panel, self-administered online, fielded each August–September). The survey moved from telephone to this online panel: APPC's own 2022 parallel run measured 72% online against 47% by phone (~25-point mode effect) and says the online years "will not be presented as part of a historical trend" with the phone years — so the phone era is a separate line (appcBranchesPhone) and the two are never joined. The 2022 value here is that parallel online reading.
meta.method: transcribed from APPC topline PDFs (read 2026-08-31): 2023 topline CIVI4 table (2023 + 2022 online panel), 2025 topline 'Number of Branches Correctly Recalled' table (2024, 2025)

meta.name: Can Name All Three Branches (phone era)
meta.unit: percent of adults naming all three branches (telephone survey)
meta.source: Annenberg Public Policy Center, Constitution Day Civics Survey
meta.note: Same question as appcBranchesWeb, asked by telephone (RDD/CATI, ~1,000–1,400 adults) from 2006 through 2022. The series ends in 2022 when APPC moved to its online panel; APPC's 2022 parallel run (47% phone vs 72% online) measured a ~25-point mode effect, which is why the eras are separate series. Not asked 2007–2010 or 2012.
meta.method: transcribed from the CIVI3/CIVI4 summary table, p.2 of APPC's September 2022 appendix PDF (read 2026-08-31)
